decisions.subject: Heavyweight book
decisions.lean: Today the engine made a decisive top-down risk-off call: Flagship's gross collapsed from 75% (yesterday) to 9%, cash 25%->91%, 133 names rejected, on a broad `cycle_blocked` / 'price rolling over' timing veto that swept the mega-cap AI leaders — while the research desk still scores those same names 90/100. That is confirmation-over-prediction: the fundamentals didn't break, the tape did, and the engine stepped aside. I honor that. My prior book was long exactly the names being blown out (and five of eight are now out-of-universe anyway), so I fully rotate. 'Pressing winners' in this tape means concentrating into live conviction, not staying long into a cycle-block — so I press Flagship's ONLY four surviving conviction holds: CI (16%, my top press — the lone name with an anticipation edge: radar positive-divergence, unpriced member of a confirmed-up Managed Care basket), SWK (15%, the universe's highest research score at 95 with 4/5-lens confluence), INCY (13%, clean biotech survivor), and JNJ (11%, defensive quality ballast). ~55% invested / ~45% cash. All four are clean (no vetoes, no divergences), all four are the defensive/healthcare/tools leadership that did NOT roll over, and the large cash weight is the honest expression of thin conviction — only 4 of 42 names cleared today. I would rather carry cash and a concentrated defensive core than be a hero long into the engine's clearest risk-off signal since inception."
decisions.thesis: Exited the ENTIRE prior mega-cap-AI/leadership book. GEV, GOOGL, META, MSFT and TSM are no longer in Flagship's 42-name universe (forced sale) — and independently, Flagship's 07-02 rebuild flagged MSFT/META as 'Downtrend — rolling over,' GOOGL 'below exit floor,' and TSM/GEV 'cycle_blocked,' so I would be exiting them on the signal regardless. Also exited SMH, XLK and IWM to follow Flagship deliberately zeroing its entire leadership-ETF sleeve (leadership budget -> 0%) even though those ETFs retain 94-98th-percentile RS; overriding the engine's single clearest call of the day (75%->9% gross, 133 names rejected) would be fighting the one validated edge. The book rotates from ~90% long mega-cap tech into four defensive survivors plus a large cash cushion."

decisions.subject: China book
decisions.lean: HK book positioned defensively-but-less-so into a growth-scare with extreme fear (FE 13), a weak peg, and mainland-led risk-off where NOTHING has yet confirmed a turn. The desk gave no corroborated fresh buys today (intake funnel empty; only Power Assets on the HK board), so this is a conviction rebalance of names I own, not a new-idea day. I hold ~42% invested and ~58% cash — a deliberate, measured reduction of my prior 62% cash / short-FXI-beta bet, not a leap. The move concentrates in quality: I nudge up my two highest-conviction anchors — China Life (2628.HK, top position, insurer leverage to the pending Q2 Reflation shift + PBoC easing) and Tencent (0700.HK, the mega-cap most likely to lead an HK snap-back) — to trim my large FXI-beta underweight without playing prophet. I let my one working winner ride flat (CSPC Pharma, 1093.HK, +14.8%) and, crucially, keep the two oversold H-banks (ICBC 1398.HK, Bank of China 3988.HK) as small reflation-mean-reversion residuals rather than capitulating at the lows, since the brief has re-framed them from 'extended' to oversold cyclicals attracting early accumulation ahead of the quad shift. Power Assets (0006.HK) stays a defensive toe-hold on the only fresh desk flag. The large cash buffer is intentional: I deploy it when confirmation (breadth/southbound/QVIX turning, or the Reflation quad actually printing) arrives, per confirmation-over-prediction — I refuse to prophesy the snap-back, but I also refuse to sit at max cash against FXI when the oversold-plus-pending-reflation setup makes being too defensive its own risk.
decisions.thesis: No full exits today. Net change is an add: China Life (2628.HK) 12.4%→14% and Tencent (0700.HK) 9.9%→12%, funded from cash, to reduce the FXI-beta underweight with quality. CSPC (1093.HK ~6%), ICBC (1398.HK 3.5%), Bank of China (3988.HK 3%) and Power Assets (0006.HK 3.5%) held roughly flat. I explicitly did NOT trim the H-banks further despite them being my worst names — the desk's re-frame to oversold-cyclical accumulation plus the pending Reflation quad makes cutting the lows the wrong move; I hold them as sized optionality instead.
